severity_name: SEVERE SLOP WARNING — COGNITIVE SATURATION ADVISORY
headline: SEVERE SLOP WARNING: BRAIN-ROT LOOP FRONT NOW OCCUPIES ONE IN FIVE CLIPS SERVED TO NEW ARRIVALS AS ENDLESS SYNTHETIC SLUDGE REELS CYCLE THROUGH COLORS, GOO, AND UNRESOLVABLE SATISFACTION AT VOLUMES DESIGNED TO OUTLAST THE HUMAN ATTENTION SPAN
advisory: The Service is tracking a persistent low-pressure loop system saturating first-contact feeds, where roughly every fifth clip presented to a newly arrived viewer is now synthetic filler engineered to be watched but never remembered. Residents are advised that the system produces no plot, no author, and no exit, only a smooth downhill gradient toward the next autoplay. The scroll may feel productive; it is not. Ground your thumb before proceeding.

regional_outlook.conditions: Dense loop cover from horizon to horizon, with pockets of glossy sludge cascading over a rim that recedes as you approach. Visibility into original content near zero before noon.
Squalls of near-identical 'relaxing' apps, each promising to reverse the very fog it is made of. Expect drizzle of five-star reviews written in the same voice.
Standing pools of auto-generated explainers filling in beneath the fold. Water table of actual answers continues to drop.
Blowing volume-count with reduced visibility; titles accumulating faster than any reader can shelf them. Chapter numbers reset without warning.
Gusty reply loops and recycled outrage forming dust devils over stale threads. Wind out of nowhere in particular, sustained.

specimen.status: Overabundant and expanding; now a dominant ground cover of the video basins
specimen.habitat: First-contact feeds, autoplay corridors, and the fifteen-second gap between one thing and the next
specimen.field_marks: A hypnotic, seamless loop of pouring, peeling, slicing, or mixing that never resolves into a result; captions promise 'wait for it' but there is no it. Colors saturate past any natural pigment. No maker is credited, because none is required.
specimen.call: Wait for it… wait for it… wait for it…
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a genuine oddly-satisfying craft video made by a real person. Distinguish by the ending: authentic craft resolves into a finished object; the Sludge Reel loops back to its own beginning, having produced nothing but another loop.

spotter_tip: If, after ninety seconds of watching, you cannot say what you saw, who made it, or why it stopped mattering the instant it ended — you were not watching content, you were being poured over. Set the device down and go look at something with edges.
tomorrow: Loop cover persists overnight; brief clearings possible wherever a resident deliberately searches for a specific human by name.

confirmed_sighting.report: A new research study reports that AI slop and 'brain rot' videos now account for roughly 20 percent of clips served to new viewers, prompting fresh questions about originality and the creator economy.
